quote: I just got a few questions to start up on your design. Is that okay?
stewart_read: Rep establishes company name but skips the interest question entirely, moving straight into qualifiers without ever anchoring why the customer should care.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be intentional compression for a short call, but the interest question is a required verify item and was never revisited later, so this reads as an omission, not a deliberate sequencing choice.
coaching_implication: Ask 'what interested you in solar' early — it gives an emotional anchor to fall back on later when the bill-collection stall hits.

quote: Their interface is less than ideal here.
stewart_read: Customer openly vents about app friction; rep says nothing empathetic and lets her keep struggling silently.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may not have registered this as an actionable friction signal versus just customer venting.
coaching_implication: This is the trigger point to pivot to verbal read-back per the schema's alternative_path — a one-line acknowledgment plus offering to just read numbers over the phone would have saved minutes.

quote: Could you screenshot, like, the last three months?
stewart_read: Rep escalates the ask to three months even though the customer has already spent 4+ minutes failing to find one month's yearly data — no protocol pivot attempted.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be a deliberate attempt to get a fuller usage picture for design accuracy, but timing (after visible struggle) makes this look like rigid script-following, not strategy.
coaching_implication: When a customer is visibly struggling past the 2-minute mark, the schema calls for a pivot to verbal readback or deferring to the specialist, not raising the ask.

quote: If you could just screenshot the last two months, I think we'll be okay.
stewart_read: Even after the customer surfaces a specific number ($6.99 -- likely hundreds, garbled in transcript) the rep doesn't reflect it back or use it to build urgency; he just downgrades the document ask.
coaching_implication: The captured bill figure ('about a 100') should have been flipped into a reason to act, not just filed as a data point while chasing documents.

quote: That is not something that I'm interested in doing right now.
stewart_read: Customer declines the appointment outright after the bill slog; rep accepts with a flat 'Okay' and never attempts a rebuttal or reframe.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the customer immediately cites a genuine family emergency, pushing harder in the moment may have backfired — a soft, no-pressure close may be the right call here.
coaching_implication: Even when backing off is right, the rep should anchor a concrete callback time or send a personalized follow-up referencing her stated bill/usage instead of letting the call end with no owned next step.

quote: please take me off of all inquiry list, like, updates because I think you guys have been calling me all the time
stewart_read: Customer raises a contact-frequency complaint on her way out and the rep says nothing to address or resolve it, just closes with pleasantries.
coaching_implication: This complaint should be acknowledged and actioned (confirm she'll be removed from repeat outreach) rather than ignored, per SESSION20's own precedent lesson in the schema.
